subject: Tier decomposition and feature mapping playbook for ClearPath pilot

Subject: Packaging options for our three product lines (Compact vs Modular)

Evelyn — thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our leadership liked the latency numbers but procurement pushed back on how our current bundle maps to your tiers. Two asks from my side: 1) Can you outline concrete upgrade/downgrade paths if we want to move some services from Compact to Modular (we don't want to double-pay during the transition), and 2) we need a price ladder that shows seat/throughput pricing at 3 commitment points (10k, 50k, 200k tokens/mo) so we can present a single-line item to finance.

I attached our current contract so you can see the current entitlements. Also curious if a short pilot (6 weeks) gets any commit discount — procurement asked.

Thanks,

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Michelle Lopez <michelle.lopez@clearpathhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for our three product lines (Compact vs Modular)

Michelle — great to meet you yesterday. Quick reply with the high-level options and I'll follow with a detailed playbook this week.

Two pragmatic paths we recommend: 

1) Tier Decomposition (recommended for risk-averse teams): split current Compact into "Core (low-latency)" + "Batch (background)" SKU lines. Migrate traffic via prefix-based routing over 4 weeks. Billing: we pro-rate overlap weeks and offer a 10% migration credit to offset duplicate capacity for the first billing cycle.

2) Feature Mapping (recommended for fast feature rollout): map features to feature-flagged add-ons (e.g., long-chat KV cache, high-throughput embedding pool). This lets you keep a single seat SKU but enable feature bundles per microservice. No double-billing during the pilot — we issue temporary feature credits.

Pilot discount: for a 6-week controlled pilot we can offer a temporary 15% commitment discount if you sign an MOU that converts to a 12-month agreement on the same tier family within 60 days.

I'll attach a one-pager and a draft token ladder. Ben will chime on capacity/throughput constraints. Jordan will own the formal quote.

Best,
--
Evelyn Hart
Director, Account Strategy — Redwood Inference
evelyn.hart@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood_feature_map_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 34KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Michelle Lopez <michelle.lopez@clearpathhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Mar 2027 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging options for our three product lines (Compact vs Modular)

Michelle — quick technical note to make the playbook realistic from an infra standpoint: 

- Seat pooling across regions is possible but affects peak latency for conversational workloads; recommend isolating the Core low-latency pool to a dedicated cluster.
- For your embedding-heavy analytics pipeline, use burstable Dedicated pools to avoid throttling; we can set a soft cap with auto-burst credits.
- If you choose Feature Mapping, we need a controlled rollout with KV cache warmup windows (we typically recommend 48–72 hours per service).

I'll attach our capacity matrix with example throughput bands so you can map the 10k/50k/200k buckets to instance types.

Cheers,
--
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Attachment: capacity-matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 86KB)

Thanks Ben — that helps. A couple of procurement constraints to call out so your quote matches what they will approve: 

- Procurement requires a single-line purchase item per legal entity if possible (they don't like many line-items across multiple clusters).
- They prefer a clear rollback path (if we go Modular and need to revert some services back to Compact within 90 days, show the financial impact).
- For the pilot billing we need an explicit clause that temporary feature credits will be applied as a single credit line on invoice rather than multiple refunds.

Can Jordan draft a ladder that expresses the 3 commitment points as single invoice lines with optional add-on toggles? If you can indicate the dollar-per-token numbers and the pro-rate rules for mid-cycle changes that would speed procurement sign-off.

Also looping in Procurement here.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Packaging options for our three product lines (Compact vs Modular)

Michelle — thanks for the clarity. Attached below is a short summary and proposed single-line ladder that procurement can accept. Highlights: 

- Single invoice line per product family combining base seat + optional feature toggles. The quote includes three committed tiers: 10k tokens/mo ($0.006/token), 50k tokens/mo ($0.0045/token), 200k tokens/mo ($0.0035/token).
- Migration credit: 10% applied to first invoice for overlapping capacity during migration (max 8 weeks).
- Rollback protection: if you reduce committed tier within 90 days we apply a one-time grace credit equal to pro-rated unused commitment (note: this resets any promotional discounts).
- Pilot clause: for a 6-week pilot we'll apply temporary feature credits as a single credit line on the invoice; if you execute the 12-month MOU within 60 days, the 15% discount is applied retroactively to pilot consumption and the credit converts to a prepayment credit.

I've started a proposal document here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1a2b3c-proposal-draft — please comment where you'd like alternate language for procurement. If that looks good I can convert to a single-line PO template and send a formal quote via DocuSign.

Next steps we propose: 
- Michelle/procurement: confirm preferred committed tier for pilot and sign MOU by Apr 6.
- Redwood: deliver PO template + formal quote by Apr 8.

I'll put Jordan's signature but Jordan is me (Account Exec).

Best,
--
